segments.text: Okay, let me widen this with questions, our face-off.
Why disallow the Cockroach Janata Party's Tiranga Yatra is the question of the day.
Are these protests hurting the government's image, particularly when young people get detained?
And the question I keep asking, is there an end game at the moment?
If so, what is it?
Sanju Verma, the national spokesperson of the BJP is joining me.
Anish Gawande of the NCP SP.
It was from Anish's house that Abhijit Deepke was detained.
Sanju Verma, let's be very clear.
Do you believe that all of this that is happening is damaging the government's image somewhere?
That if you are so strong, if you have no fear, why detain, arrest, latte, charge the young?
Those optics, are they looking good?
Rajdeep, Abhijit Dikke had asked for permission for Jantar Mantar 1.0 in Delhi in July.
That permission was given.
Abhijit Didke asked for permission at Shivaji Park on the 2nd of October on Gandhi Jayanti.
That permission was given.
Abhijit Didke asked for permission that his CJP colleagues should be allowed to protest at Mumbai's Azad Maidan today.
That permission was given.
Of course, yes, it's a different matter that there were hardly 25 to 30 people.
And the public has completely abandoned the CJP in Mumbai.
That's not the moot point.
The moot point is this.
We are not a banana republic.
We are run by the law of the land.
Beat Abhijit, Dipke, Ashutosh, Ranka, Saurabh Das.
Nobody is above the law of the land.
One section 163 of the BNS is in place.
And Dipke, Das, and Ranka have signed a bail bond
saying that they will not breach peace.
It is incumbent upon them to not breach the provisions of their bail bond.
How is it breaching peace, ma'am?
Just clarify.
How is it breaching peace if he wants to do a Tiranga march?
How does that breach peace?
Rajdeepji, I thought you would let me speak for at least a minute without interjecting.
But let me answer that.
I knew you would ask me this question.
You are so predictable.
But could you ask me this?
Jantar Mantar 1.0.
The CJP had promised, assured the Delhi police, no incendiary slogans, no political activity, no caste-based slogans will be raised.
And social media is viral with these videos.
Rajdeep, Modi margaya hai hai.
I want to ask Rajdeep Sardesai, Samvidhan ko aag laga do is a peaceful slogan?
I haven't heard Abhijit Dipke give any of these slogans.
None of these slogans that you have put on the TV channel today have been said by Abhijit Dipke.
Have any of them been said?

When Abhijit Dipke is sharing stage with Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, Shabana Azmi and a whole lot of other Aam Aadmi party leaders like Kejriwal, Sisodia, what have you, and these slogans are raised, the Delhi Commissioner of Police Mr. Deepak Purohit, again another DCP Mr. Sachin Sharma, tell Abhijit Dipke, tell Saurabh Das, tell Ashutosh Ranka, please do not carry on with this protest because we believe that
There are criminal elements who have infiltrated the protest.
What do these three people say?
You become conveniently deaf, dumb, blind and mute when it is the other side which is wearing the wrong shoe on the wrong foot.
I am neither deaf, dumb
or blind, not yet.
And I have full respect for India's disabled.
But Anish Gawande, respond to what you're hearing.
Has the CJP lost its way?
A movement that claimed that it was coming to represent the concerns of Gen Z, exam irregularities, school ko sudaro, improve schools, has suddenly moved now into a political battle.
And when you do that,
When are you losing your way?
Was Abhijit Dipke's protest today simply spectacle politics?
Let's get eyeballs rather than really about the Tiranga Yatra.
Rajiv, you know I didn't want to come on this show today and the reason for that was very simple.
It's because the pathetic moral cowardice of a government that dares to detain three of my friends twice over the course of a week is on full display.
The pathetic moral cowardice of a government that beats up young people, chokes young women with their dupattas,
who hacks and kicks young men and women on their private parts is on full display.
This is moral cowardice, and it must be understood as such.
Whether you agree with this Tiranga Yatra or not is irrelevant.
The fact that Abhijit was going alone, that he told the police that he was going alone is important.
He was not violating 144, now 163.

When you go as a single individual onto the streets with a tricolor on your hand, under which law is the government of the day putting you behind bars, taking you round and round in a police van and detaining you?
Under what law is a government that says, har ghar tiranga, preventing har sadak tiranga from taking place?
This is cowardice.
They say the apprehension of violence, the apprehension that the CJP was going to use this Tiranga Yatra perhaps to incite violence.
Rajdeep, I would love to believe that this government cares about violence.

But today at Karnot Place, you have journalists pointing out hecklers, people with sticks in their hands, not being apprehended by the same police force that picks up innocent people who are there with a tricolour.
A few days ago, you saw the Hindu Kranti Dal proudly claiming that we got bail this evening, while Ashutosh and Saurabh go to Tihar for five days.
I mean, the Bharatiya Janata Party has to ask itself this question.
The people of India are watching.
This pathetic cowards will no longer fly, Rajdeep.
And how will you allow it to happen?
And I want to just say one thing here.
This protest has been Gandhian for a reason.
Gandhi marched alone.
And you will know this because many of us know Ramdas Bhattkar in Mumbai.
And I learned from him, much like many others in Mumbai have.
But at Noakhali, Gandhi marched alone.
When the British in 1940 engaged in similar repression, he announced the individual Satyagraha.
And Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first Satyagrahi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was the second.
And so this regime will also face similar protests.
But July 20th, you will recall, Anish, July 20th turned violent.
July 20th protest turned violent.
So the police will always use that as a reference point.
And Rajsi, can you tell me why those protests on the 20th of July turned violent?
Why were CCTV cameras disabled?
Why was checking stopped at entry and exit points?
Why were barricades welded into each other?
Why has no action still been taken against anybody who was violent?
And why has action not been taken against the police officers who were seen shoving rods into the private parts of young women?
Rajdeep, what an atrocious denial of accountability by a shameless government.
No, no, man, you must listen.
Just a minute.
Anish, I've heard you.
I have heard you.
You made very strong point.
You see, Sanju Verma, we all want to listen to each other.
I want to listen to you.
I want to listen to Anish.
You see, these are very serious observations.
Even what has happened today, today it seemed that the traders of Karnat Place were being used to target perhaps the Cockroach Janta Party or people who wanted to march peacefully.
My problem is if this is such a mighty government as it is,
Right?
What are you afraid of?
What are you afraid of?
What can Abhijit Dipke do to the mighty government of the BJP, the largest party in the world?
Why do you need the police to then resort to these repressive measures, even though the Supreme Court, Sanju Verma, had said that they have the right to protest and take out this march?
They did not, High Court did not stop them.
Rajdeep, I heard that it's a lengthy question.
Rajdeep Sardesai had been trying since May 2014.
Rajdeep Sardesai couldn't do anything.
Please don't attack the messenger.
Madam, please don't attack me.
It's unfair.
I asked you a question.
Reply to it without bringing me into it.
I am not involved.
You can respond to Anish Gawande.
You are not involved now.
Don't get rattled.
He said moral cowardice.
He says your government is showing moral cowardice.
Respond.
Rajdeep, do not interject.
I heard Aneesh Gawande.
I'm not hard of hearing.
And let me tell you, when I called you deaf, dumb, and mute to the hard reality, I was not being unfair to the especially abled.
That was a metaphor.
Please understand the metaphor.
Thank you.
Now let me respond to Aneesh Gawande.
What is moral cowardice?
Moral cowardice is when Abhijit Dipte says that he's bigger than the law of the land.
Moral cowardice is when Rahul Gandhi
holds DK Shiv Kumar by the scruff of his neck.
Moral cowardice is when Priyanka Vadra shoves her elbow into the breast and stomach of a female police constable.
Moral cowardice is when Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka, without an iota of proof, keep saying that the election commission is a criminal enterprise.
Moral cowardice is when ACP Vivek Bhagat is falsely accused of molesting
a female journalist by showcasing an AI-generated video?
I want to ask one question.
Article 19, which gives the right to protest, Article 19, does not have rights under Article 19?
Madam, are you really seriously on this show comparing the asymmetry of power between the police with Lathis and citizens who are unarmed?
Madam, you have raised various questions.
You have accused Priyanka Gandhi, Vadra and others.
All of this should be an inquiry.
You know, you're making these allegations.
But are you seriously comparing a police which is well armed with unarmed protesters?
Is that a serious comparison to make?
You know Rajdeep, what I don't understand, when Anish was speaking, I did not see you interjecting him even once.
So let me tell Anish Govande.
One thing, please now.

Moral cowardice is when Sharath Pawar's NCP loses its national party status in 2023, and their spokesperson has the audacity to lecture the Modi government, which has won three Lok Sabha elections in a row.
This is the problem.
When Sharath Pawar's party did not even get 22 seats, and BJP had a strike rate of 91% in Maharashtra elections, but Sharath Pawar's spokesperson sits here
and lectures on constitutional propriety to the BJP, that is moral cowardice.
But my final point... Isn't there a difference between election results and what happens on the street, ma'am?
Rajiv, you have a great memory.
You have a great memory.
And I say this to many off-record, on-record, for whatever it is worth.
In 2022, two incidents happened.
A young engineering student called Mikhil Bhamre was picked up from his residence in Nashik for simply sharing a meme on Sharad Pawar.
And a young Marathi actress called Ketaki Chitale shared an innocuous meme on Sharad Pawar.
She had 22 FIRs against her.
And my final point, you know this very well.
There is a civil engineer called Anant Karmuse.
He was kidnapped, beaten, abducted by Jitendra Awar, the close confidant of Sharad Pawar.
Shame on you.
You know, that's a... I take your point, these are all water-mow tree, but, you know, Anish Gawande, you want to respond.
Anish Gawande, you want to respond.
The fact at the end of the day, the one point that the BJP keeps making, whatever you want to do at the end of the day, do it through the ballot.
You want... If you believe that this government has failed, then fight them on the ballot.
By taking it to the streets, you're actually trying to create extra constitutional methods to target the Modi government, a final point.
The same Bharatiya Janata Party that learned from Ram Manohar Lohia must remember his famous saying,

The reason the streets are live with the voice of the people, Rajdeep, is because, and I will say this purposely so Sanju Verma today gets agitated again because she thinks our voice does not matter and the voice of the BJP is the only thing that matters.
Rajdeep, this is a regime change operation and regime change in a democracy is called a no confidence motion.
Their allies will lose confidence in them.
Members of the Bharatiya Janata Party will lose confidence in them.
This is a moral battle fought on Mahatma Gandhi's principles.
Even the oppressor will realise that their oppression is no longer valid and that's why we will hit the streets.
They will detain one, they will detain another.
I've listened to you, Anish, and I've listened to you, Sanju Verma.
Thank you very much, Sanju Verma and Anish Gawande for joining me on the show.
No, Madam, I have some time, 30 seconds for my take on this special.
State versus the street.
It's been a turbulent week in Indian politics, with the battle moving from Parliament and television studios to the streets of this country.
But here's a fundamental democratic principle.
Protest is not a threat to democracy.
It is a safety valve that keeps democracy alive.
The state has every right, indeed a duty, to maintain law and order.
But there is a crucial distinction between preventing violence and criminalizing dissent.
or picking up someone from their house or an aircraft when they have not committed any crime.
Detaining protesters, arresting young activists, shutting down public spaces cannot become the default response to what is primarily a political disagreement.
Peaceful protest is a constitutional right, not a favour granted by the government.
The test of a democracy is not how efficiently it can silence its critics, but how confidently it can accommodate them.
When the state begins to see every gathering as a law and order problem, it risks turning a legitimate democratic demand into a confrontation.
The state must maintain order, but not at the cost of liberty.
A democracy should fear violence, not peaceful dissent.
And yes, whether there is a regime change or not,
will not be decided in the end with street protests.
It will be decided by the ballot box.
Let's leave it in the end to Janata Janardhan.
But at least respect the Janata of this democracy of ours.
And only then can we call India a true mother of democracy.
Think about it.
Thanks very much for watching.
Stay well.
Stay safe.
Have a safe festive weekend.
Jai Hind.
Namaskar.
